summary: npm package hosts an obfuscated Microsoft-login phishing redirector
details: The package's only artifact is an HTML page that impersonates a Cloudflare Turnstile 'security verification' challenge. On Turnstile callback, heavily obfuscated JavaScript (obfuscator.io-style string array with a custom base64 decoder and console-method overrides for anti-debug) reconstructs a target URL whose visible literal fragments include 'gin.micros' and 'online.com', then calls window.location.replace() on it, forwarding all incoming query-string parameters — a Microsoft-login credential phishing lure. The package declares no lifecycle scripts and no JS main, so `npm install` does not execute code on the installer's machine; instead the package abuses the npm registry as content-hosting infrastructure for a phishing page. Obfuscation of the redirect destination combined with a fake Turnstile UI is an evasion pattern warranting registry takedown.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
